verses.1:1: And the word of the Lord came to Micah the son of Morasthi in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, concerning the things he saw regarding Samaria and regarding Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: Hear words, O peoples, and let the earth give heed, and all who are in it; and the Lord, the Lord shall be among you for a witness, the Lord from His holy house.
verses.1:3: For behold, the Lord comes forth from His place, and He shall descend upon the high places of the earth,
verses.1:4: and the mountains shall be shaken beneath Him, and the valleys shall melt like wax before the face of fire, and like water carried down a steep descent.
verses.1:5: All these things are because of the ungodliness of Jacob, and because of the sin of the house of Israel. What is the ungodliness of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the sin of the house of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
verses.1:6: And I will make Samaria a watchman's hut in a field and a planting of a vineyard; and I will drag down her stones into a chasm, and I will uncover her foundations.
verses.1:7: And all her carved images they shall cut to pieces, and all her hires they shall burn with fire, and all her idols I will give over to destruction; because from the hires of harlotry she gathered them, and from the hires of harlotry she amassed them.
verses.1:8: Because of this she shall beat her breast and lament; she shall walk barefoot and naked; she shall make lamentation like that of dragons and mourning like that of the daughters of sirens;
verses.1:9: for her wound has prevailed, because it has come even to Judah and has reached even to the gate of My people, even to Jerusalem.
verses.1:10: You who are in Gath, do not magnify yourselves; you who are in Akim, do not rebuild from a house a mockery; sprinkle yourselves with dust for your mockery.
verses.1:11: Dwelling well in her cities, she who dwells in Sennaar did not come forth to mourn the house adjoining her; she shall receive from you a stroke of grief.
verses.1:12: Who has begun for good toward her who dwells in sorrows? For calamities have come down from the Lord upon the gates of Jerusalem,
verses.1:13: a sound of chariots and horsemen. O inhabitant of Lachish, she is the leader of sin to the daughter of Zion, for in you were found the impieties of Israel.
verses.1:14: Therefore she shall give those who are sent away even to the inheritance of Gath, vain houses; they have come to nothing for the kings of Israel,
verses.1:15: until they bring the heirs, O inhabitant of Lachish; an inheritance shall come even to Adullam, the glory of the daughter of Israel.
verses.1:16: Shave yourself and cut off your hair for your delicate children; enlarge your widowhood like an eagle, because they have been carried away captive from you.
verses.2:1: They became devisers of troubles and workers of evil upon their beds, and at the break of day they accomplished them, because they did not lift up their hands to God.
verses.2:2: And they coveted fields, and plundered orphans, and oppressed houses, and plundered a man and his house, even a man and his inheritance.
verses.2:3: Therefore thus says the Lord: "Behold, I am devising calamities against this tribe, from which you shall by no means lift up your necks, and you shall by no means walk upright suddenly, for it is an evil time."
verses.2:4: In that day a proverb shall be taken up against you, and a lamentation shall be lamented in song, saying, "With misery we have been made miserable; the portion of my people has been measured out with a line, and there was no one to hinder him from turning away; our fields have been divided."
verses.2:5: Therefore you shall have no one casting a line by lot in the assembly of the Lord.
verses.2:6: Do not weep with tears, nor let them shed tears over these things; for he shall not cast off reproaches,
verses.2:7: he who says, "The house of Jacob has provoked the Spirit of the Lord." Are these His practices? Are not His words good with him, and have they not walked uprightly?
verses.2:8: And formerly My people rose up in enmity; opposite his peace they flayed off his skin, so as to take away hope, the shattering of war.
verses.2:9: The leaders of My people shall be cast out from the houses of their luxury; because of their evil practices they have been driven out. Draw near to the everlasting mountains.
verses.2:10: Arise and depart, for this is not your rest because of uncleanness. You have been corrupted with corruption,
verses.2:11: you have been pursued when no one pursues; a spirit has established falsehood, it has dripped for you for wine and strong drink. And it shall come to pass from the drop of this people,
verses.2:12: Jacob shall surely be gathered with all; I will surely receive the remnant of Israel, together I will appoint his return; like sheep in affliction, like a flock in the midst of their fold, they shall leap forth from among men.
verses.2:13: Through the breach before their face they broke through, and passed through the gate and went out through it; and their king went out before their face, and the Lord shall lead them.
verses.3:1: And he shall say: "Hear now these things, O rulers of the house of Jacob and you remnant of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice,
verses.3:2: who hate good things and seek evil things, who tear their skins from them and their flesh from their bones?
verses.3:3: Just as they devoured the flesh of my people, and flayed their skins from them, and crushed their bones, and cut them in pieces like flesh for a cauldron and like meat for a pot,
verses.3:4: so they shall cry out to the Lord, and He will not hear them; and He will turn away His face from them at that time, because they acted wickedly in their practices against them."
verses.3:5: Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace upon him, and when nothing was put into their mouth, they raised up war against him:
verses.3:6: "Therefore night shall be to you without a vision, and darkness shall be to you without divination; and the sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall grow dark over them;
verses.3:7: and those who see dreams shall be put to shame, and the diviners shall be mocked, and all of them shall speak against them, because there shall be no one who hears them."
verses.3:8: Unless I fill up strength by the Spirit of the Lord, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his impieties and to Israel his sins.
verses.3:9: Hear now these things, O leaders of the house of Jacob and you remnant of the house of Israel, who abhor justice and pervert all things that are upright,
verses.3:10: who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices.
verses.3:11: Her leaders judged for bribes, and her priests answered for hire, and her prophets divined for silver; yet they rested upon the Lord, saying, "Is not the Lord among us? Calamities shall by no means come upon us."
verses.3:12: Therefore because of you Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall be like a watchman's hut, and the mountain of the house shall become a grove of the forest.
verses.4:1: And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, made ready upon the summits of the mountains, and it shall be lifted high above the hills; and peoples shall hasten to it.
verses.4:2: And many nations shall go and say, "Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob; and they will show us His way, and we shall walk in His paths." For from Zion a law shall go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
verses.4:3: And He shall judge between many peoples, and rebuke mighty nations even far away; and they shall cut down their swords into plows, and their spears into sickles; nation shall no longer lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn to wage war anymore.
verses.4:4: And each one shall rest beneath his vine, and each one beneath his fig tree, and there shall be no one to terrify them; for the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things.
verses.4:5: For all the peoples shall walk each in his own way, but we shall walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.
verses.4:6: "In that day," says the Lord, "I will gather her who has been crushed, and her who has been driven out I will receive, along with those whom I cast off.
verses.4:7: And I will make her who has been crushed into a remnant, and her who was cast off into a mighty nation; and the Lord shall reign over them on Mount Zion from now even forevermore."
verses.4:8: And you, gloomy tower of the flock, daughter of Zion, to you it shall come; even the former dominion shall enter in, a kingdom from Babylon to the daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.4:9: And now, why have you known evils? Was there no king for you? Or has your counsel perished, that birth pangs have seized you like a woman in labor?
verses.4:10: Be in travail, and take courage, and draw near, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth; for now you shall go out from the city, and encamp in the plain, and come even to Babylon; from there the Lord your God shall deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.
verses.4:11: And now many nations have been gathered against you, saying, "We shall gloat over her, and our eyes shall gaze upon Zion."
verses.4:12: Yet they did not know the design of the Lord, and did not understand His counsel, that He has gathered them like sheaves of the threshing floor.
verses.4:13: Arise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns of iron, and your hooves I will make of bronze; and you shall melt down many peoples, and you shall dedicate their multitude to the Lord, and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
verses.4:14: Now the daughter shall be hedged in with a hedge; he has laid a siege against you; with a rod they shall strike upon the cheek the gates of Israel.
verses.5:1: And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, you are very small to be among the thousands of Judah; out of it shall come forth to Me One to be Ruler of Israel, and His goings forth are from the beginning, from the days of eternity.
verses.5:2: Therefore He shall give them up until the time when she who is in labor shall give birth; and the rest of their brethren shall return to the sons of Israel.
verses.5:3: And He shall stand and look, and the Lord shall shepherd His flock in strength, and they shall abide in the glory of the name of the Lord their God; for now He shall be magnified to the ends of the earth.
verses.5:4: And this shall be peace: when Asshur comes against your land, and when he treads upon your country, then seven shepherds and eight bites of men shall be raised up against him.
verses.5:5: And they shall shepherd Asshur with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in its trench; and He shall bring deliverance from Asshur when he comes against your land, and when he treads upon your borders.
verses.5:6: And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like dew falling from the Lord, and like lambs upon the grass, so that no one may be gathered together nor withstand among the sons of men.
verses.5:7: And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts in the forest, and like a young lion among flocks of sheep, just as when he passes through, and separating them, snatches them away, and there is no one to deliver.
verses.5:8: Your hand shall be lifted up over those who afflict you, and all your enemies shall be utterly destroyed.
verses.5:9: "And it shall come to pass in that day," says the Lord, "I will utterly destroy the horses from your midst and demolish your chariots.
verses.5:10: And I will utterly destroy the cities of your land and remove all your strongholds.
verses.5:11: And I will utterly destroy your sorceries out of your hands, and there shall be no soothsayers among you.
verses.5:12: And I will utterly destroy your carved images and your pillars from your midst, and you shall no longer worship the works of your hands.
verses.5:13: And I will cut down the groves from your midst and obliterate your cities.
verses.5:14: And I will execute vengeance in wrath and in fury upon the nations, because they did not listen."
verses.6:1: Hear now a word. The Lord, the Lord has said, "Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice."
verses.6:2: Hear, O peoples, the judgment of the Lord, and you ravines, foundations of the earth; for the Lord has a controversy with His people, and He will contend with Israel.
verses.6:3: O My people, what have I done to you, or how have I grieved you, or how have I troubled you? Answer Me.
verses.6:4: For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you from the house of bondage; and I sent before your face Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
verses.6:5: O My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised against you, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, from the rushes even to Gilgal, so that the righteousness of the Lord might be known.
verses.6:6: With what shall I reach the Lord, and lay hold of my God Most High? Shall I reach Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
verses.6:7: Will the Lord accept thousands of rams, or ten thousands of fat torrents? Shall I give my firstborn for ungodliness, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
verses.6:8: Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to practice justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?
verses.6:9: The voice of the Lord shall be proclaimed to the city, and He shall save those who fear His name. Hear, O tribe! And who shall adorn the city?
verses.6:10: Is there not fire, and the house of the lawless man storing up lawless treasures, and unrighteousness with insolence?
verses.6:11: Shall the lawless man be justified with a balance, and with weights of deceit in a bag?
verses.6:12: From these they have filled their wealth with ungodliness, and its inhabitants spoke lies; and their tongue—be exalted in their mouth.
verses.6:13: And I will begin to strike you; I will lay you waste in your sins.
verses.6:14: You shall eat, and shall by no means be satisfied; and it shall grow dark within you, and it shall turn aside, and you shall by no means be saved; and as many as are saved shall be delivered over to the sword.
verses.6:15: You shall sow, and shall by no means reap; you shall press the olive, and shall by no means anoint yourself with oil, and wine, and you shall by no means drink it; and the ordinances of My people shall be wiped out.
verses.6:16: And you have kept the statutes of Zimri and all the works of the house of Ahab, and you have walked in their ways, so that I should deliver you over to desolation and its inhabitants to hissing; and you shall bear the reproaches of the peoples.
verses.7:1: Woe is me, for I have become like one who gathers stubble in the harvest, and like gleanings in the vintage, when there is no cluster to eat the first-ripe fruits. Woe is me, O soul,
verses.7:2: for the godly man has perished from the earth, and there is no upright one among men; they all contend in judgment for blood, each one oppresses his neighbor with oppression;
verses.7:3: they prepare their hands for evil. The ruler asks, and the judge has spoken words of peace; it is the desire of his soul. And I will take away their good things
verses.7:4: like a moth devouring and walking upon a measuring line in the day of watching. Woe, woe, your acts of vengeance have come; now shall be their weepings.
verses.7:5: Do not trust in friends, and do not put your hope in leaders; guard yourself from her who lies with you, lest you entrust anything to her;
verses.7:6: for a son dishonors his father, a daughter will rise up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; all those in a man's house are his enemies.
verses.7:7: But I will look to the Lord; I will wait patiently for God my Savior; my God will hear me.
verses.7:8: Do not gloat over me, O my enemy, because I have fallen, yet I shall rise again; for even if I sit in darkness, the Lord will give light to me.
verses.7:9: I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against Him, until He vindicates my cause; and He will execute my judgment, and You will bring me forth into the light; I shall behold His righteousness.
verses.7:10: And my enemy shall see it, and she shall be clothed with shame—she who says to me, "Where is the Lord your God?" My eyes shall look upon her; now she shall be for trampling down like mire in the streets.
verses.7:11: In the day of plastering brick, that day shall be your blotting out, and that day shall wear away your ordinances;
verses.7:12: and your cities shall yield to leveling and to division among the Assyrians, and your fortified cities to division from Tyre to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to the mountain;
verses.7:13: and the land shall become a desolation together with those who dwell in it, from the fruits of their practices.
verses.7:14: Shepherd Your people with Your rod, the sheep of Your inheritance, who dwell by themselves in a forest in the midst of Carmel; they shall graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
verses.7:15: And according to the days of your departure from Egypt, you shall behold wondrous things;
verses.7:16: the nations shall see and be put to shame even because of all their might; they shall lay their hands upon their mouth, their ears shall become deaf,
verses.7:17: they shall lick dust like a serpent, crawling upon the earth; they shall be confounded in their confinement; they shall be astounded at the Lord our God, and they shall be afraid of You.
verses.7:18: Who is a God like You, taking away iniquities and passing over ungodly deeds for the remnant of His inheritance? And He has not held fast His wrath for a testimony, because He delights in mercy.
verses.7:19: He will turn again and have compassion on us; He will submerge our unrighteous deeds, and they shall be cast into the depths of the sea—all our sins.
verses.7:20: He will give for truth to Jacob, mercy to Abraham, just as You swore to our fathers according to the former days.

notes.1:1: The Greek renders the Hebrew gentilic 'the Morashtite' as a patronymic, 'the son of Morasthi' (ton tou Morasthei).
notes.1:8: The Greek text uses the third person singular ('she shall beat her breast') referring to Samaria, and renders the mourning creatures as 'dragons' (drakonton) and 'daughters of sirens' (thygateron seirenon).
notes.1:10: The Septuagint preserves the distinct proper name Akim (where the Hebrew reads 'weep not') and interprets the wordplay on Beth-le-aphrah as rebuilding a mockery from a house.
notes.1:11: The Greek reads the place name Sennaar (corresponding to Hebrew Zaanan) and translates the Hebrew place names Shaphir and Beth-ezel descriptively as 'dwelling well' and 'the house adjoining her.'
notes.1:16: The Greek text reads 'widowhood' (cherian) rather than 'baldness' found in the Hebrew text and some later manuscripts.
notes.2:1: Where the Hebrew explains the wicked deeds by saying it is in the power of their hand, the Greek reads 'because they did not lift up their hands to God.'
notes.2:8: The Greek diverges notably from the Hebrew garment imagery, describing the people as flaying off skin 'opposite his peace' so as to strip away hope through 'the shattering of war.'
notes.2:12: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew term for a sheepfold (Botzrah) as 'in affliction' (en thlipsei), emphasizing Israel's distress before deliverance.
notes.3:1: The Greek opens in the third person future ('And he shall say') and addresses 'the remnant' (hoi kataloipoi, also in 3:9) where the Hebrew refers to rulers.
notes.3:8: The Greek begins with ean me ('unless'), a literal rendering of the Hebrew adversative particle ('but truly'), contrasting the prophet's empowerment by the Spirit of the Lord with the silenced false prophets of 3:7.
notes.3:12: As in 1:6, the Greek translates the desolation of Jerusalem with oporophylakion ('a watchman's hut' in an orchard or field) rather than 'heaps of ruins.'
notes.4:2: The Greek has a third-person plural verb ("they will show us"), whereas the Hebrew text reads singular ("He will teach us").
notes.4:8: The Greek describes the tower as "gloomy" (auchmodes) and uniquely adds "from Babylon," a phrase absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.4:14: The Greek text reads "the gates (pylas) of Israel," where some Greek manuscripts read "tribes" (phylas) and the Hebrew text reads "judge."
notes.5:1: The Greek reads "house of Ephrathah" and the relative pronoun "out of it" (ex hou), whereas other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew text read "out of you."
notes.5:4: "Eight bites of men" reflects the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew word for "princes" from a similar root meaning "to bite."
notes.5:6: The Greek reads "like lambs upon the grass," whereas the Hebrew text reads "like showers upon the grass."
notes.6:5: "From the rushes" translates the Greek common noun schoinon, where the Septuagint rendered the Hebrew place name Shittim as a botanical term.
notes.6:7: "Fat torrents" translates the Greek cheimarron pionon, corresponding to the Hebrew "rivers of oil."
notes.6:8: The Greek begins with a passive question ("Has it been declared to you") and reads "to be ready to walk" rather than the Hebrew "to walk humbly."
notes.6:12: The Greek text contains the passive imperative "be exalted" (hypsotheti), reflecting a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew calls the tongue "deceitful."
notes.6:16: The Greek text names "Zimri" (Zambrei), a Septuagint-distinct proper name where the Hebrew text reads "Omri."
notes.7:3: The Greek reads "the judge has spoken words of peace" and "I will take away their good things" (continuing into 7:4 with "like a moth devouring"), diverging notably from the Masoretic Text's reference to bribery and a brier hedge.
notes.7:9: The Greek shifts abruptly to the second person in "You will bring me forth into the light" (ἐξάξεις) between third-person references to the Lord, a distinctive Septuagint reading preserved here.
notes.7:11: The Greek renders this verse as a judgment oracle concerning "plastering brick" and the "blotting out" of the city and its ordinances, contrasting with the Masoretic Text's promise of rebuilding walls.
notes.7:18: The Greek reads "for a testimony" (εἰς μαρτύριον), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew consonants as "witness" rather than "forever."
notes.7:20: The Greek reads third-person "He will give for truth" (δώσει εἰς ἀλήθειαν) before shifting to second-person "just as You swore," preserving a notable Septuagint textual feature.
